acquisition_method.evidence: The mass spectrometer was operated in “top-15” data-dependent mode

cleavage_agent.evidence: Protein concentration was measured using the Tryptophan assay and 300 µg were further processed for overnight digestion by adding Lys-C and trypsin in a 1:50 ratio (µg of enzyme to µg of protein) at 37 °C and 1700 rpm.

collision_energy.evidence: Following higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) with a normalized collision energy (NCE) of 27%, MS/MS spectra were collected in the Orbitrap

fractionation_method.evidence: About 30 µg of peptides of each sample were further fractionated into 54 fractions and concatenated into 8 fractions by high-pH reversed-phase fractionation using the recently described “loss-less” nano-fractionator.

fragmentation_method.evidence: Following higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) with a normalized collision energy (NCE) of 27%, MS/MS spectra were collected in the Orbitrap

instrument.evidence: Nanoflow LC–MS/MS analysis of tryptic peptides was conducted on a quadrupole Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Q Exactive HF, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Rockford, IL, USA)

ionization_type.evidence: coupled to an EASYnLC 1200 ultra-high-pressure system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) via a nano-electrospray ion source.

labeling.evidence: Label-free quantification was performed with the MaxLFQ algorithm using a minimum ratio count of 1.

mass_analyzer.evidence: Nanoflow LC–MS/MS analysis of tryptic peptides was conducted on a quadrupole Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Q Exactive HF, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Rockford, IL, USA)

ptm.evidence: peptides with a minimum length of seven amino acids with carbamidomethylation as a fixed modification, and N-terminal acetylation and methionine oxidations as variable modifications.
